newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes fall tracking WTI/Cushing.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes fall tracking WTI/Cushing.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices fell sharply Thursday tracking WTI/Cushing prices following the closing of an Alaskan crude deal on Wednesday that saw BP sell a cargo to a Pacific Northwest refiner, traders said.

The cargo, weighing 300,000 barrels, cost $1.18 under benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI). The deal, confirmed by both parties, posted a 12 cent-increase over the last cargo, which sold Tuesday at a discount of $1.30.
Some traders said the higher ANS price might be reflective of tightness in the Northwest rather than in California where crude supplies have backed up amid refinery problems.

Four producers of California heavy crude -- Mobil, Arco, Texaco, and Monterey Resources -- continued to look for ways to sell-off 1.2 million barrels of heavy crude after Tosco force majeured the volume last week.
One of the producers said they would get rid of supply by sending 250,000 barrels to their Panama refinery.
The last heavy deal was done Friday at $1.00 under postings, compared with sales of 25 to 50 cents earlier that week.
Confirmed prices for San Joaquin Valley heavies ranged $17 to 17.25 a barrel, flat from Tuesday.
